questions.q: In an oxygen-free sewer, which organisms produce hydrogen sulfide gas?
distractors: Algae growing on the pipe walls

questions.q: What do these H2S-producing microbes use to break down organic matter?
How does adding calcium nitrate cut H2S production?
questions.answer: Nitrate-reducing bacteria outcompete the H2S producers for organic carbon
distractors: The nitrate chemically neutralises H2S gas into water
Calcium coats the concrete so H2S cannot touch it
The nitrate kills every bacterium in the sewer

questions.q: Why do nitrate-reducing bacteria win that competition?
questions.answer: They have a higher affinity for nitrate than the H2S producers have for sulfate
distractors: They consume sulfate faster than the H2S producers
They are the only bacteria that survive without oxygen
They release an acid that dissolves the H2S producers

questions.q: How does hydrogen sulfide actually damage concrete pipes?
questions.answer: It reacts with moisture to form sulfuric acid, which degrades the concrete
distractors: It freezes inside the pores and cracks the concrete
It raises the gas pressure until the pipe bursts
It dissolves the steel reinforcement directly

questions.q: At what point does calcium nitrate stop the corrosion?
questions.answer: At the source: it stops H2S being produced, so no acid forms
distractors: After the damage: it repairs acid-eaten concrete
In the air: it dilutes the sulfuric acid
On the surface: it seals the pipe wall
